messages:
Maya (oncall): Heads-up — saw another p95 spike on text-gen yesterday around 02:10 UTC. Looks like the same cache-warmup pattern we saw two weeks ago. Opening thread to align on SLO tweak + action owners.

Ian: Saw it in the traces too. CPU on the batching head node spiked when a big fanout request hit. Suspect prefix cache miss + bursty traffic.

Priya: Can we confirm whether it was a single customer or multi-tenant? If single, might be rate-limit gaps. If multi, routing/fallbacks.

Maya (oncall): Preliminary: 60% of the requests were from promo traffic (multi-tenant). No single huge token count. Dashboard screenshot: https://redwood.dev/dash/latency/abcd123

Sam: Reposting alert query we used yesterday for reference:
```
sum by(route) (rate(request_latency_p95_seconds{env="prod"}[5m]) > 0.5)
```
This still trips during the bursts.

Jordan: Recommend short-term SLO change: increase p95 target from 350ms -> 450ms for 48h to buy breathing room while we patch batching head autoscale and add prefix caching. Thoughts? :thinking_face:

Priya: I'm +1 for a temporary SLO window but we should document it as an opt-in rollback for customers on Dedicated. Also need error-budget guardrails so we don't eat into long-term SLAs.

Ian: Operational items I can pick up: adjust horizontal autoscale policy for batching-head (threshold 70% -> 55%), add a cooldown of 60s, and add metric to the runbook. ETA: EOD today.

Maya (oncall): Priya — can you own the SLO change + communication (status page blurb + internal console note)? Owner: Priya. ETA: 2 hours. Include the canary flag for Dedicated customers.

Priya: Will do. Draft note: "Temporary p95 lat target increase to 450ms for 48h in prod due to recurring cache-warmup bursts. Dedicated customers may opt-out; contact support." I'll post on statuspage and update the SLO dashboard.

Sam: I'll add a dashboard panel showing prefix cache hit ratio and a histogram of request token sizes. Action: Sam, ETA 6h.

Jordan: Longer-term: schedule model-variant fallback policy so when a heavy request arrives we route to a lower-cost variant instead of overloading batch head. I can draft RFC. Owner: Jordan, ETA 2 weeks.

Maya (oncall): Ops-Bot, please create a follow-up ticket list and assign the items: autoscale tweak (Ian), SLO comms (Priya), cache panel (Sam), RFC (Jordan).

Ops-Bot: Created ticket REDW-3421 with subtasks: REDW-3422 (autoscale) -> Ian, REDW-3423 (SLO change & comms) -> Priya, REDW-3424 (cache panel) -> Sam, REDW-3425 (variant fallback RFC) -> Jordan. Due dates set per owners.

Priya: Quick note on error budget — propose we mark this 48h window as "maintenance override" and exclude it from monthly burn calculations, otherwise we risk false alarms. Anyone object?

Ian: No objection, but record clearly in the postmortem that this is an exception.

Maya (oncall): Agreed. After autoscale change and dashboard updates, let's reconvene in 48h for a quick check-in and then close or extend. I'll schedule a 15min sync: 1767940000 (48h).

Sam: FYI adding the histogram requires a small query tweak, ping me if you want to test.

Jordan: I'll start RFC skeleton today and add migration plan for model variants.

Maya (oncall): Thanks all — good actionability here. Will attach this thread to the incident postmortem and mark owners in the tracking board. :thumbsup:

Priya: Posted status page and updated SLO dashboard note. Link: https://status.redwood.dev/incidents/REDW-3421

Ian: Autoscale rolling change deployed to canary cluster, monitoring p95.

Sam: Cache panel live in the ops dashboard. Initial read: cache-hit dipped to 28% during spike.

Maya (oncall): Logged recon: 48h check-in scheduled, owners assigned in REDW-3421. Closing thread for async follow-up — please update tickets as you make progress.

Jordan: Thanks — will update RFC draft tomorrow.

Ops-Bot: Reminder scheduled: 1767940000 — "48h SLO check-in for cache-warmup incidents"
